options.text: The transport of dissolved sugars and amino acids through phloem
The evaporation of water from leaves
The absorption of minerals from soil
The movement of water in xylem

questions.explanation: Translocation is the movement of dissolved organic substances, mainly sucrose and amino acids, through the phloem from sources (where they are made) to sinks (where they are used or stored).

options.text: Sieve tube elements and companion cells
Root hair cells
Xylem vessels
Guard cells

questions.explanation: Phloem tissue consists of sieve tube elements (which form the transport tubes) and companion cells (which provide energy and metabolic support for transport).

questions.stem: How are sieve tube elements different from xylem vessels?

options.text: Sieve tubes are living cells with sieve plates; xylem vessels are dead and hollow
There is no difference
Sieve tubes are dead; xylem is alive
Sieve tubes have lignin walls

questions.explanation: Sieve tube elements are living cells (though they lack a nucleus) with perforated end walls called sieve plates. Xylem vessels are dead, hollow, and reinforced with lignin.

questions.stem: What is a source in translocation?

options.text: A part of the plant that produces or releases sugar, such as photosynthesising leaves
A part of the plant that uses sugar
The flowers only
The roots only

questions.explanation: A source is any part of the plant that produces or releases sugars, such as leaves that are photosynthesising, or storage organs that are releasing their stored sugars in spring.

questions.stem: What is a sink in translocation?

options.text: The leaves only
A part of the plant that uses or stores sugar, such as roots, fruits, or growing tips
A part of the plant that produces sugar
The stomata

questions.explanation: A sink is any part of the plant that uses or stores sugar, such as growing roots, developing fruits, storage organs accumulating starch, or meristems where cells are dividing.

options.text: It does not require energy
Because sugars are loaded into phloem by active transport, using ATP from companion cells
Because phloem is made of dead cells
Because water must be pumped upward

questions.explanation: Translocation is an active process. Sucrose is loaded into sieve tubes by active transport, which requires ATP provided by the many mitochondria in companion cells.

questions.stem: What is the role of companion cells in phloem?

options.text: To provide energy (ATP) for loading sugars into sieve tubes and to support sieve tube function
To photosynthesize
To absorb water
To produce lignin

questions.explanation: Companion cells have many mitochondria to produce ATP via respiration. This energy is used to actively load sucrose into sieve tube elements and to maintain the metabolic functions of the living phloem tissue.
